stem: An engineer wants to use an AWS provider configured with an alias (such as aws.west) inside a child module to manage resources in an alternate region. How should the child module declare this requirement according to Terraform conventions?
options: In the child module's terraform.required_providers block, declare the alias name inside configuration_aliases.
In the parent module's module block, declare configuration_aliases = ["aws.west"] alongside source.
In the child module's main.tf, define a new provider "aws" block configured with alias = "west".
In the child module's variables.tf, declare an input variable of type provider default = "aws.west".
objective: Explain how provider inheritance functions between parent and child modules, including configuration_aliases

stem: A team is refactoring infrastructure into multiple child modules located in the modules/ directory. Where should the primary provider "aws" configuration blocks be defined?
options: In a shared provider.tf file placed directly inside the modules/ directory outside any child module.
Inside an environment-specific child module that exports the provider via an output value.
In each child module's main.tf, so that every child module remains self-contained with its own provider block.
In the root module, because child modules automatically receive their provider configurations from their parent modules.
objective: Explain how provider inheritance functions between parent and child modules, including configuration_aliases

stem: You are organizing a Terraform repository following the standard module structure. Which layout correctly adheres to the standard hierarchy?
options: Create arbitrary sibling directories at the repository root for each module without using a modules/ subdirectory.
Keep the repository root empty and place all configurations and root files into a src/ root directory.
Place all child module resources into a single modules.tf file in the repository root without separate directories.
Store root module configuration files (main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf) in the repository root, and place nested child modules under the modules/ subdirectory.
objective: Organize infrastructure configurations into root modules and child modules located in modules/ directories
